scenes.title: Melzack and Wall demonstrating the fast-touch vs slow-ache spinal gate diagram beside a bumped-shin reflex
scenes.era: 1965, MIT neurophysiology seminar room, Cambridge, Massachusetts

layout.description: Sunlit 1965 MIT laboratory-seminar room featuring a slate chalkboard drawn with the classic three-box Gate Control circuit ('L' large fibers, 'S' small fibers, 'SG' gate, 'T' transmission) beside a demonstration bench with a handheld TENS-prototype nerve stimulator.

positions.who: Ronald Melzack (mannequin in 1965 tweed blazer and tie)
positions.where: standing at the chalkboard pointing chalk to the '+' inhibitory gate arrow from large 'L' touch fibers

positions.who: Patrick D. Wall (mannequin in rolled white lab shirt sleeves)
positions.where: seated on the bench edge placing a small round tactile stimulator pad onto his own forearm to demonstrate pain gating

props.name: 1965 Gate Control chalkboard schematic
props.period_detail: crisp white chalk diagram showing Large fibers (+), Small fibers (-), Substantia Gelatinosa (SG), and Transmission cell (T)
props.physical_behavior: illustrates how fast touch closes the gate before signals ascend

props.name: prototype benchtop tactile nerve stimulator
props.period_detail: 1960s brushed-metal low-voltage pulse box wired to two small round skin pads on Wall's forearm
props.physical_behavior: delivers gentle high-frequency buzz recruiting thick A-beta touch fibers

props.name: myelinated vs unmyelinated cable model
props.period_detail: two physical tabletop nerve rods — one thick insulated rod and one thin bare wire
props.physical_behavior: visualizes the 100 m/s vs 1 m/s conduction speed gap

actions.verb_sequence: presses a blunt pressure gauge against his forearm -> switches ON the gentle A-beta tactile buzz pad right beside it -> nods as perceived sharpness drops immediately
traces the chalk line from Large 'L' touch fiber into the 'SG' spinal gate blocking the 'T' output

reactions.reaction: rotates his forearm comfortably while the tactile buzz runs
caps the chalk diagram with the top-down 'Central Control' arrow from the brain

scenes.wardrobe: 1965 MIT academic dress: Melzack in herringbone jacket, white shirt, narrow dark tie; Wall in rolled Oxford sleeves, dark trousers, lab coat draped on chair.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key New England laboratory daylight across slate chalkboard and brushed aluminum instruments.
scenes.recognition_hook: Buzzing thick touch nerves on his own forearm at MIT, Patrick Wall proves you can physically slam a gate inside the spinal cord before pain ever reaches the brain.

key_visual.description: two 1965 MIT neuroscientists beside a 'L / S / SG / T' Gate Control chalkboard diagram testing a small round tactile nerve-stimulator pad on a bare forearm

scenes.title: Universal bumped-shin rub recruiting fast A-beta fibers

layout.description: Sunlit living room where a person mannequin bumps a shin lightly against a low wooden coffee table and immediately rubs the spot briskly with both palms.

positions.where: sitting on sofa edge briskly rubbing shin right above the bumped spot

actions.verb_sequence: bumps shin on oak corner -> immediately rubs surrounding skin firmly -> posture relaxes within seconds

reactions.reaction: exhales as fast touch signals outrun and gate the slow ache

scenes.recognition_hook: Rubbing a bumped shin isn't superstition — it fires 100 m/s touch cables to close the spinal gate.

scenes.title: Athlete finishing a championship play before noticing a scrape

layout.description: Bright indoor basketball court sideline after the final buzzer.

positions.where: celebrating at the buzzer, then glancing down in surprise at a scraped knee

props.name: scoreboard reading 00:00
props.physical_behavior: marks the moment intense top-down focus releases

actions.verb_sequence: lands final shot in full focus -> walks to bench after buzzer -> only then notices the knee scuff

reactions.reaction: hands an ice wrap as descending brainstem gating steps down

scenes.wardrobe: Clean white-and-navy athletic jersey and shorts.
scenes.recognition_hook: Top-down brainstem signals can hold the spinal gate closed until the crisis or game ends.

scenes.title: Combining gentle warmth/touch and slow breathing during a vaccine shot

layout.description: Clean bright clinic chair where a patient presses cool tactile vibration near the shoulder while breathing slowly instead of staring tensely.

positions.where: seated relaxed with dropped shoulders breathing slowly
applying a small vibration/cool pack beside the deltoid

actions.verb_sequence: places gentle vibrating cool pack above the site -> Patient breathes out slowly

reactions.reaction: blinks in pleasant surprise that the pinch barely registered

scenes.wardrobe: Modern casual t-shirt and clean clinical scrubs.
scenes.recognition_hook: Pairing local touch buzz with relaxed breathing closes the spinal gate from bottom-up and top-down at once.
